name: Baked Ground Beef Stroganoff Casserole

ingredients.name: neutral cooking oil, such as canola or vegetable oil, divided
unsalted butter, plus more for greasing baking dish

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 205°C (400°F). Grease a 13- by 23-cm baking dish with butter; set aside.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil over high heat. Add noodles and cook according to package directions until just shy of al dente, about 6 minutes. Drain and rinse under cool running water; set aside.

Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, whisk 1 tablespoon water with baking soda until dissolved. Add ground beef and gently mix until thoroughly combined; set aside. In a 2-cup liquid measuring cup or medium bowl, whisk together broth and gelatin; set aside.

In a Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, until well browned, 12 to 15 minutes. Reduce heat to medium and add shallots, butter, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt. Cook, stirring frequently, until shallots are softened, about 2 minutes. Add thyme, 2 teaspoons paprika, and 1 teaspoon black pepper and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add wine, increase heat to medium-high, and bring to a simmer. Cook, scraping up any browned bits from bottom of Dutch oven, until wine is almost completely evaporated, about 5 minutes. Transfer mushroom mixture to a large bowl. Wipe Dutch oven clean.

Heat remaining 1 tablespoon oil in Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add beef mixture and remaining 1 teaspoon kosher salt and cook, stirring occasionally and breaking beef into small pieces with a wooden spoon, until well browned and almost cooked through, 5 to 7 minutes. Add tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, until slightly darkened, about 2 minutes.

Add broth and gelatin mixture to Dutch oven and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, scraping up any browned bits from bottom of Dutch oven. Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, whisk together sour cream, Worcestershire sauce, and Dijon mustard. Gradually whisk 3/4 cup simmering broth mixture into sour cream mixture. Remove Dutch oven from heat and stir in mushroom mixture, tempered sour cream mixture, and noodles until evenly combined. Transfer to prepared baking dish and spread into an even layer.

In a small bowl, stir together panko, Parmesan, and remaining 1/4 teaspoon each paprika and black pepper. Sprinkle evenly over casserole. Bake, uncovered, until topping is browned and casserole is bubbling around edges, about 15 minutes. Let casserole rest for 15 minutes. Garnish with parsley and serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: beef stroganoff recipe, ground beef casserole recipe, Ground Beef Stroganoff Casserole

description: This make-ahead ground beef Stroganoff is a creamy, mushroom-packed 9x13 casserole finished with a crisp Parmesan-panko topping.
notes:
Make-ahead and storage: The casserole can be assembled through step 6, covered, and refrigerated for up to 4 days. Prepare the panko topping and refrigerate it in a separate airtight container. When ready to bake, cover the casserole with aluminum foil and bake at 205°C (400°F) until hot throughout, then remove the foil, add the topping, and continue baking until browned and bubbling around the edges.
To freeze, assemble the casserole through step 6 and let it cool completely. Cover tightly with plastic wrap and aluminum foil and freeze for up to 2 months; freeze the topping separately. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before baking as directed above. Freezing may leave the noodles slightly softer.
Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days. To reheat the entire casserole, cover with foil and bake at 175°C (350°F) until heated through, 20 to 30 minutes. Uncover for the final 5 to 10 minutes to recrisp the topping. Individual portions can be reheated in the microwave, though the topping will lose some of its crunch.
author: Leah Colins
